name: Why Students Miss School
title: Why Students Miss School
answer: Attendance data records how many days a student missed, not why. The reasons vary widely, from illness and transportation to bullying, anxiety, family care, and disengagement, and each needs a different response. A person must follow up to learn the reason and choose the right action, while AI can only help categorize recorded reasons and show trends.

sections.body: Attendance numbers alone cannot explain an absence. A student may be absent because of illness, a broken bus route, bullying, anxiety, caring for family members, or disengagement. These causes call for different responses, and a reminder message will not solve a transportation problem or a fear of a classmate. The idea is to have a person follow up, learn the actual reason, and match the response to it. Schools can then track the reasons they find to see patterns and guide larger fixes.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, an attendance worker might arrange transportation, a counselor might address anxiety, or a teacher might reconnect a disengaged student with a class they enjoy. The text does not give separate grade bands, so the same approach applies across grades. Schools can record the reasons staff discover and look for patterns across the district. Those patterns can guide larger changes, such as bus schedules or health services. AI can help sort the reasons staff record into categories and highlight trends, but it does not replace the conversation.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no evidence label, study, figure, or finding for this idea. It rests on practice rather than research. The book presents the approach as a practical response to attendance data and does not cite research to support it.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: AI should not guess the reason for any individual student's absence. Guesses based on data can stereotype students and families. Only a conversation reveals what is really happening. The decision about how to respond stays with a person, such as an attendance worker, counselor, or teacher. The text sets these limits clearly, so AI remains a sorting and trend tool, not a judge of any student's situation.
